get.description:
Your captured sessions in this workspace. Every filter applies before
paging.

- `state` (repeatable) keeps sessions whose `display_state` is one of the
  given values, derived exactly as each item reports it.
- `status` filters on the session's own lifecycle: `active` means an event
  in the last 15 minutes, `idle` a longer silence, and `ended` an end
  event or a day of silence.
- `q` matches title, repository, branch or board name, case-insensitively
  and literally (`%` and `_` are not wildcards).
- `linked_only` keeps sessions that touched a card or note you can see.
- `since` keeps sessions active at or after that instant.
- `root_only` hides subagent threads (sessions that declared a parent).
- `sort`: `recent` (last activity, the default), `started`, `duration`
  (first to last event), `tokens` (input, output and cache), or `cost`
  (the effective cost whatever its basis; sessions without one last).
  Largest or newest first.

Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` with the same `sort`; a cursor from
another sort is rejected.

Totals across your sessions in this workspace that match the same
filters as the list: how many, how many are live, the wall time they
cover (overlaps once), tokens, and cost per basis. The API-equivalent
and spend amounts are separate and never add up to one figure.

get.description:
The loop template catalog: system templates then workspace templates.

Entries are SUMMARIES — prompts, slots and tool grants live behind
`GET /{ref}`, because the Library page renders none of them and a catalog
that inlined five full prompt pairs would ship tens of kilobytes per view.

`meta` carries the runner var vocabulary so the prompt-var palette never has
to hardcode it.

post.description:
Create a draft template (version 0, nothing published yet).

Deliberately NOT idempotent: a repeated slug returns 409 rather than the
existing row. The idempotency rule exists for calls agents retry, and
templates are authored by humans — silently returning someone else's
template under the slug this author chose would discard their content
without either author seeing a conflict.

Import a `loop_template` envelope as a DRAFT in this workspace.

Declared BEFORE `/{ref}`: FastAPI matches in declaration order, so the
literal path has to win or "import" would be read as a template ref.

`dry_run=true` (the default) previews the action and mutates nothing — the
destructive half of a share is opt-in over HTTP, matching the pipeline
bundle route. A commit always lands unpublished, so importing a file can
never change what a running board executes; publishing stays a separate
act. Wrong envelope → 400; a template that cannot render → 422.

schema.title: Response Import Loop Template Api Workspaces  Slug  Loop Templates Import Post

get.description:
One template in full. `ref` is a system slug or a workspace row UUID.

`?draft=true` serves the unpublished half, which is what the manager edits;
an unpublished template serves its draft either way, since it has no
published half to show.

patch.description: Autosave the draft half under an optional `expected_updated_at` lock.

get.description: Published history, newest first.

get.description:
The template's profile page — stored identity plus derived track record.

Archived templates are included: a board bound before the archive still
links here, and its history is the reason the page exists.

post.description:
Render `ref` with no board in sight — the template author's own check.

POST rather than GET because the slot values are a document, not a query
string: a block slot legitimately carries a multi-kilobyte prompt fragment.
It stays a READ — nothing here writes, and it is member-gated for the same
reason the fit report is.

Values fall back through `default` then `example`, so an author who has
filled neither sees the slot left literal and named in `missing_required`,
rather than a prompt that quietly pretends to be complete.

Validate the draft, snapshot it, and bump the published version.

A draft that fails validation 422s with the findings attached so the
manager can deep-link the offending tab.

get.description:
Download a template as a portable `loop_template` envelope.

Member-gated like the other reads: an export copies out the artifact the
member can already read in the manager. Exporting a SYSTEM template is
allowed and marked `is_system_origin` — it is the natural way to fork a
shipped loop.

post.description:
Scan a template's kernel for facts that belong in slots (spec F12).

Member-gated and NOT agent-banned, matching `preview` next door: nothing
here writes, and a runner checking the template it was bound to is a
legitimate reader. Always 200 — the findings are hints for a human, and an
endpoint that 422'd on them would be a control nobody asked for.
Fork any template — system or workspace — into a new workspace draft.

Soft-archive: the row leaves the listing but keeps serving bound boards.

There is no hard delete — a board bound to a deleted template would render
nothing at its next iteration.
Stage a published snapshot as the draft. It does NOT republish.

get.description:
Return the closed registry of lifecycle step kinds plus operator docs.

`kinds` drives the step editor and client-side validation (schema + flags).
`docs` carries the human-facing explanation of each kind — sibling map, keyed
by the same names, so the editor can teach what a step does. Backend remains
authoritative on both.

ActivityListRead.title: ActivityListRead
ActivityListRead.description:
`?summary=true` shape for the activity HISTORY endpoints.

ActivityRead minus the three JSONB blobs — `changes`, `before_state`,
`after_state` — which together dominate the row while the activity feed
renders only the prose. The board TIMELINE replay engine does fold the
snapshots, but it reads /timeline, which has no trimmed mode.

A separate model rather than an exclude-set so the omission shows up in
the OpenAPI schema and a future heavy field can't silently ride along.

ActivityTrendPoint.title: ActivityTrendPoint
ActivityTrendPoint.description:
One calendar day of the activity sparkline. Zero-count days are present
as real points — the chart is fixed-width, so a gap would misread as a dip
in a shorter series rather than a quiet day.

AgentKeyCreated.title: AgentKeyCreated
AgentKeyCreated.description: `key` is the raw API key; it is never stored and never returned again.

AgentListRead.title: AgentListRead
AgentListRead.description:
`?summary=true` shape for the agents list: AgentRead without
`sensor_catalog`, the per-heartbeat sensor manifest the runner WRITES and
no list surface renders (the frontend reads it from its own
/workspace-config sensor endpoint). Scoped to the list — /agents/me,
/agents/{id} and the heartbeat response still carry it.

Subclassed rather than redeclared: AgentRead is ~50 fields with a liveness
validator, and a hand-copied twin would drift on the next field added.
Excluding the field keeps it out of the response AND out of the OpenAPI
schema for this endpoint.

capture_level.title: Capture Level
capture_level.description: The content level this event was stored at; null when it was captured before levels were recorded.

data.title: Data
data.description: The stored Beacon event, reduced to its capture_level. `backplane_redactions` maps each withheld path to the sha256 and bytes Backplane received, and `original_bytes`: the content's size before Backplane or the companion withheld it, null when unknown, absent on events stored before it was recorded.

status.title: Status
status.description: The session's own lifecycle, from its timestamps alone (the `status` list filter): active, idle after 15 min of silence, ended on a session end event or after 24 h of silence (`ended_reason` tells which).

cwd.title: Cwd
cwd.description: The working directory, never a path of the device: the bound folder's name plus the path inside it (`backplane/packages/api`), only a folder's own name outside the mapping or at the metadata level.

reasoning_tokens.title: Reasoning Tokens
reasoning_tokens.description: Part of output_tokens spent reasoning; not added to totals.

cost_usd.title: Cost Usd
cost_usd.description: Effective USD cost: per usage report the agent-reported cost when it reported one, otherwise Backplane's API list-price estimate; null when neither exists (never 0 for unknown).

cost_reported_usd.title: Cost Reported Usd
cost_reported_usd.description: Sum of the costs the agent itself reported.

cost_estimated_usd.title: Cost Estimated Usd
cost_estimated_usd.description: Sum of Backplane's list-price estimates from vendored price tables.

cost_source.title: Cost Source
cost_source.description: Where cost_usd came from: all agent-reported, all estimated, or mixed.

cost_basis.title: Cost Basis
cost_basis.description: spend when an API key (or enterprise contract) paid; api_equivalent for a subscription or unknown login, where the cost is what the same usage would cost at API list price, not money spent. Null without a cost.

cost_complete.title: Cost Complete
cost_complete.description: False when any usage report could be neither reported nor priced.

auth_kind.title: Auth Kind
auth_kind.description: How the agent was paid for, as last seen on the session.

capture_gaps.title: Capture Gaps
capture_gaps.description: Records for this session that ingest rejected; the timeline has holes.

activity_event_count.title: Activity Event Count
activity_event_count.description: Stored events that say what the agent did: every event except token usage reports and session start or end markers.

coverage.title: Coverage
coverage.description: activity when any activity event was captured; usage_only when the agent reported token usage or cost but no activity (the Codex app, for one), which does not mean nothing happened; empty with neither. Gaps are capture_gaps and display_state, not coverage.

capture_levels.title: Capture Levels
capture_levels.description: The distinct content levels Backplane applied when it stored this session's events, least recently applied first: the last is the level of the latest capture, more than one means the level changed mid-session. A level is an upper bound on what was kept. Empty when any of the session was captured before levels were recorded; no level is claimed for it then.

display_state.title: Display State
display_state.description: Derived at read time: ended (session end event, no gaps); paused (capture switched off for this device, agent or mapping); disconnected (device revoked or silent past the heartbeat limit); otherwise active, idle after 15 min of silence, incomplete after 24 h or with capture gaps.

ended_reason.title: Ended Reason
ended_reason.description: Set exactly when `status` is ended, whatever `display_state` shows: `session_end_event`, or `abandoned` after 24 h of silence.

idle_since.title: Idle Since
idle_since.description: When the current silence began (the last event), once the session has been quiet for more than 15 minutes and has not ended.

child_count.title: Child Count
child_count.description: Subagent sessions that named this one as their parent. Null where it is not computed (the device API).

link_count.title: Link Count
link_count.description: Distinct cards and notes this session changed or consulted that still exist where you can see them. Null where it is not computed.

link_preview.title: Link Preview
link_preview.description: Up to two of those cards and notes: changed before consulted, then the most recently touched; one entry per card or note. Null where it is not computed.

AssignmentLLM.title: AssignmentLLM
AssignmentLLM.description:
Per-stage LLM dispatch info. Provider + model are backend-authoritative;
the runner must use them rather than its yaml defaults. prompt_slug
identifies which prompt template the runner should render — defaults to
the stage name when no operator override exists. tool_policy carries the
per-stage tool deny-list (empty `deny` for stages without a configured
policy).

tier carries the RAW tier name (premium/mid/low) when the stage's model is
an abstract tier — empty for a concrete/literal model. It is the
provider-agnostic intent: a runner may remap a tier to whichever local
coding agent it has via its llm.tier_providers config, treating
provider+model as the resolved hint/fallback. Empty for old configs and
pinned models; old runners simply ignore it.

AssignmentSkill.title: AssignmentSkill
AssignmentSkill.description:
One entry of the board's effective skills manifest on the wire.

Sync contract: mirrored by `AssignmentSkill` in
runner/internal/valaris/client_skills.go (decoded by client.go) — the two sides
change in the same commit. Wire fields are exactly what the runner needs
to materialize and report a skill bundle: slug/name/description for the
agent-facing catalog, version + content_hash to fetch and verify the
published files. Board-authority fields (skill_id, enabled,
pinned_version, role) deliberately stay off the wire. Additive: old
runners simply ignore it.

AssignmentToolPolicy.title: AssignmentToolPolicy
AssignmentToolPolicy.description:
Backend-authoritative tool deny-list for the stage's LLM subprocess.

`deny` holds claude-CLI tool/Bash-pattern strings (e.g.
`Bash(gh pr merge:*)`) the autonomous agent must NOT run. The strings are
opaque to the backend — it carries them verbatim; the runner applies them
as `claude --permission-mode bypassPermissions --disallowedTools <entries>`.
This is the security floor that protects the review gate (no self-merge,
no force-push, no push-to-main). Deny-only — there is no allow-list.

AutoMappingRequest.title: AutoMappingRequest
AutoMappingRequest.description:
`repo_url` may be raw or already normalized. The device sends no local
path: it keeps the repository's root on the machine.

BlockSpan.title: BlockSpan
BlockSpan.description: Half-open UTF-8 byte offsets of one exact block occurrence.

BoardBaseline.title: BoardBaseline
BoardBaseline.description:
The board's CURRENT state, used by the timeline engine to SEED the fold
(contract v1.1). Columns/cards are the role-agnostic snapshot dicts produced
by snapshot_column / snapshot_card — columns ordered by position, cards the
flat list across every column.

BoardCardDistribution.title: BoardCardDistribution
BoardCardDistribution.description:
Cards per column_type. `untyped` holds cards in columns with no
column_type set, so the buckets always sum to the board's card_count.

BoardDependencyEdge.title: BoardDependencyEdge
BoardDependencyEdge.description:
One directed edge for the board-level tree view: `card_id` depends on
`depends_on_card_id`. Bare ids — the client already holds the card data.

BoardSkillBindingPut.title: BoardSkillBindingPut
BoardSkillBindingPut.description:
Binding update where BOTH fields are tri-state on the wire: an
OMITTED field leaves the stored value unchanged (a pin-only PUT must not
re-enable a disabled skill, and an enabled-only PUT must not unpin),
while `pinned_version: null` EXPLICITLY unpins back to tracking the
latest published version. Distinguished via `model_fields_set`; the
`enabled` default applies only when the PUT creates the binding.

exclude_globs.title: Exclude Globs
exclude_globs.description: fnmatch patterns matched on the server against the mapping's repository URL (`host/owner/repo`) and each event's working directory relative to the mapping root (`.` for the root itself); `*` also crosses `/`. The device also applies them to local paths before capture.

retention_days.title: Retention Days
retention_days.description: Delete this device's sessions this many days after their last event; null keeps them until the owner deletes them.

CardDependencyRead.title: CardDependencyRead
CardDependencyRead.description:
Wire shape for one card_dependencies row.

`depends_on_*` projections are denormalised for the scheduler-friendly
detail view (no client-side N+1). The list_for_card endpoint fills them
via a single bounded join.

CardFormat.title: CardFormat
CardFormat.description:
Wire format for a single card read. `prosemirror` (default) returns the
stored description; `markdown` serializes it back to CommonMark.

CardSummary.title: CardSummary
CardSummary.description:
Browse-view card WITHOUT description, participants, or derived ballast.

Returned by the search endpoint when `?summary_only=true`. A label query on
a busy board returns full CardRead payloads well past 100KB — enough to
overflow an MCP client's token budget on what is meant to be a cheap triage
scan. The retained fields are exactly what a caller needs to decide which
card to fetch in full: identity, where it sits, and how it is classified.

`position` is part of that decision, not ballast: the documented triage rule
breaks priority ties by lowest position, and omitting it sent agents back to
the unsummarised payload for ordering alone — defeating the projection.

ChannelListRead.title: ChannelListRead
ChannelListRead.description:
`?summary=true` shape for the channels list: ChannelRead without the
unbounded `metadata_json` blob, which no list surface renders and the
channel editor never round-trips on save.

ConflictInfo.title: ConflictInfo
ConflictInfo.description:
A card in a done-typed column that still depends on at least one card
that is NOT in a done-typed column — an unsatisfied prerequisite on
something already marked done.

ConnectionCheck.title: ConnectionCheck
ConnectionCheck.description: One verified duty and what to do when it is not satisfied.

ContentAck.title: ContentAck
ContentAck.description:
The server's answer to one declaration. `available`: the body is
durable (or there is none to send). `recorded`: the metadata is kept but
no body will be accepted (`coverage` says why, e.g. quota). Both, and
`dropped` (deleted history) and `rejected`, let the device delete its
spooled body; `upload_required` keeps it until the upload is available.

ContentBodyPage.title: ContentBodyPage
ContentBodyPage.description:
`GET …/contents/{id}/body?offset=` for text: at most
MAX_BODY_PAGE_BYTES, cut on a UTF-8 boundary.

ContentError.title: ContentError
ContentError.description: The app's error envelope (app/main.py) with the content codes.

ContentRead.title: ContentRead
ContentRead.description:
One content item as its owner reads it. `render`: `text` pages through
/body, `image` may be shown inline from /download, `download` is offered
as a file only, `none` has no body (see coverage).

ContextAdmission.title: ContextAdmission
ContextAdmission.description:
Budgeted admission of one source's bounded candidate window.

Counts cover the selected window only; a more-candidates sentinel is
metadata, never a candidate, and no unobserved tail count is invented.

ContextBindingRead.title: ContextBindingRead
ContextBindingRead.description: The authorized assignment identity an execution was started under.

ContextBudgetReport.title: ContextBudgetReport
ContextBudgetReport.description:
Effective policy and what this assembly spent. The invocation limit is
carried for the final prompt+system gate; assembly does not enforce it.

ContextDiagnostics.title: ContextDiagnostics
ContextDiagnostics.description:
Whole entries bounded by count and serialized UTF-8 bytes; the counts
always cover every exclusion in the inspected windows.

ContextDispatchStamp.title: ContextDispatchStamp
ContextDispatchStamp.description: The context-dispatch floor negotiated for an assignment or start.

ContextExclusion.title: ContextExclusion
ContextExclusion.description:
One candidate left out whole. Header-only exclusions carry no rendered
size or revision; a non-note block has no note identity.

ContextReceiptRead.title: ContextReceiptRead
ContextReceiptRead.description:
One retained invocation snapshot. `prepared`/`not_verified` records the
input the caller declared, not proof that a provider ran or used it.

ContextReceiptSummary.title: ContextReceiptSummary
ContextReceiptSummary.description: History row: no prompt bodies and no manifest.

ContextRecord.title: ContextRecord
ContextRecord.description: One selected note occurrence, hashed over the exact bytes it rendered.

ContextSource.title: ContextSource
ContextSource.description:
One configured context source, in configuration order.

`record_traced` sources list every admitted record; `source_only` sources
carry the hash of their whole rendered block and no record provenance.

CostCircuitBreakerConfig.title: CostCircuitBreakerConfig
CostCircuitBreakerConfig.description:
Workspace-level cost circuit breaker settings.

`action` decides what happens when the rolling-window spend exceeds
`threshold_usd_per_15min`:
  - "alert"      : emit cost.threshold_crossed only.
  - "pause"      : also short-circuit /next-assignment with 423 Locked.
  - "kill_runner": pause + emit a runner-shutdown event (NOT YET WIRED;
    treated as "pause" until the kill-runner handler lands).

CycleInfo.title: CycleInfo
CycleInfo.description:
One strongly-connected component of >=2 mutually-reachable cards (a
self-loop is impossible — the model's CHECK constraint forbids it).

web_origin.title: Web Origin
web_origin.description: The web app's origin (`scheme://host[:port]`), for links the device opens; null when the server has none configured.

DeviceMappingCreate.title: DeviceMappingCreate
DeviceMappingCreate.description:
A device binding a local project to a board the owner chose. Without a
`root_path` the mapping is rootless, like an auto-match: the device keeps
the repository's local root.

api_base_url.title: Api Base Url
api_base_url.description: The https origin agents the device launches should call (backplane-mcp's VALARIS_API_URL). It can differ from the endpoint the device paired against, e.g. when only /api/companion/* is reachable there. Null when the server's API URL is unset or not https; the device then keeps using its endpoint.

rich_capture.description: Present (possibly null) from rich capture's first release: null when this server offers no rich capture to this device.

exclude_globs.title: Exclude Globs
exclude_globs.description: fnmatch patterns matched on the server against the mapping's repository URL (`host/owner/repo`) and each event's working directory relative to the mapping root (`.` for the root itself); `*` also crosses `/`. The device also applies them to local paths before capture.

retention_days.title: Retention Days
retention_days.description: Delete this device's sessions this many days after their last event; null keeps them until the owner deletes them.

DeviceSettingsUpdate.title: DeviceSettingsUpdate
DeviceSettingsUpdate.description:
Retention and pausing are not here: retention is changed on the web only,
and pausing is local to the device.

DeviceStatusReport-Input.title: DeviceStatusReport
DeviceStatusReport-Input.description: The companion's heartbeat: what it is capturing and how its queue is.

DeviceStatusReport-Output.title: DeviceStatusReport
DeviceStatusReport-Output.description: The companion's heartbeat: what it is capturing and how its queue is.

DispatchPreparationCreate.title: DispatchPreparationCreate
DispatchPreparationCreate.description:
Strict: an unknown member is a 422, never silently dropped, and every
member takes part in request-key idempotency.

DispatchSettings.title: DispatchSettings
DispatchSettings.description:
Server-owned rendering inputs for one invocation. `system_template` is
always empty in v1: prompt configs carry a single content template.

ExcerptNoteCreate.title: ExcerptNoteCreate
ExcerptNoteCreate.description:
The dedicated publication route's body. Both excerpt fields are
required, so a backend without the route cannot quietly save a request
as an ordinary note.

ExcerptSource.title: ExcerptSource
ExcerptSource.description:
The captured content an excerpt save was reviewed from, each item with
the digest the owner saw.

ExecutionContextRead.title: ExecutionContextRead
ExecutionContextRead.description:
Current context for one bound active execution (same shape as the
assignment's `context` map plus its manifest and revision).

ExecutionDetailRead.title: ExecutionDetailRead
ExecutionDetailRead.description:
Single-execution detail: counts its retained context receipts rather
than embedding them (history pages through its own endpoint).

ExecutionListRead.title: ExecutionListRead
ExecutionListRead.description:
`?summary=true` shape for the executions LIST endpoints.

Identical to ExecutionRead minus `input_prompt` (the full rendered LLM
prompt) and `tool_invocations` — the two fields no list UI renders and
which dominate the payload. Declared as its own model rather than an
exclude-set on ExecutionRead so the omission is visible in the OpenAPI
schema and a new heavy field can't silently join the trimmed response.

`tool_calls_count` stays: it is a scalar column on the execution, not a
length of the dropped relationship, and the timeline renders it.

FinalizeRequest.title: FinalizeRequest
FinalizeRequest.description:
`POST /api/companion/contents/{content_id}/finalize`: the whole body's
size and digest, which must match the declaration.

Finding.title: Finding
Finding.description:
One reviewer finding. Severity drives the done-gate; file/function are
optional because not every finding is line-anchored (e.g., a missing test
file, an architectural critique).

GitConnectionPatCreate.title: GitConnectionPatCreate
GitConnectionPatCreate.description:
Operator-supplied personal access token for a forge account.

The account identity is deliberately absent: it comes from probing the
forge with the token, never from what the operator claims.

GitConnectionRead.title: GitConnectionRead
GitConnectionRead.description: Outbound representation of a git connection — never includes tokens.

HistoryDeleted.title: HistoryDeleted
HistoryDeleted.description:
This session's history under `mapping_id` was deleted through
`deleted_through`, on the device's clock: the server drops anything
observed at or before it and keeps what comes later, so the device need
not upload the former. `reason`: `owner` deleted it, or `retention`
removed it after the device's retention period.

InjectedBytes.title: InjectedBytes
InjectedBytes.description:
Distinct exact-block bytes per channel (union of spans, never a sum of
provenance rows) and their total.

InstallationEnrollment.title: InstallationEnrollment
InstallationEnrollment.description: `device_token` is present only on the response that minted it.

provenance.title: Provenance
provenance.description: exact when any of the session's links to this entity is exact.

total_duration_seconds.title: Total Duration Seconds
total_duration_seconds.description: Sum of each session's span from first to last event; a subagent thread overlapping its parent is counted in both. Prefer wall_duration_seconds for elapsed time.

wall_duration_seconds.title: Wall Duration Seconds
wall_duration_seconds.description: Elapsed time covered by at least one linked session: the union of each session's span from first to last event, so a subagent thread overlapping its parent is counted once.

cost_usd.title: Cost Usd
cost_usd.description: Sum of the sessions' effective costs; null when none has one.

cost_source.title: Cost Source
cost_source.description: Where cost_usd came from: all agent-reported, all estimated, or mixed.

cost_basis.title: Cost Basis
cost_basis.description: spend when an API key (or enterprise contract) paid; api_equivalent for a subscription or unknown login, where the cost is what the same usage would cost at API list price, not money spent. Null without a cost. mixed when the sessions differ.

cost_complete.title: Cost Complete
cost_complete.description: False when any linked session has no cost or an unpriced usage report.

LinkedWorkSummary.title: LinkedWorkSummary
LinkedWorkSummary.description: Totals across the caller's own sessions linked to one card or note.

LoopBindingDiffRead.title: LoopBindingDiffRead
LoopBindingDiffRead.description:
What changed between the version a board rendered and the current one.

Computed on demand and never stored: the bound version's content is
already reconstructible from its snapshot, so caching this would only add
a way for it to go stale against the template it describes.

An unchanged kernel is the empty string rather than a header-only diff, so
the UI can branch on falsiness instead of parsing unified-diff text.

LoopBindingRead.title: LoopBindingRead
LoopBindingRead.description:
The authoring state behind a bound board's rendered prompts.

Deliberately NOT `extra="forbid"`: later cards widen this payload (new
required slots after a template bump, whether a diff is available), and a
closed model would turn each addition into a coordinated schema change.

`drift` repeats `template.drift`'s verdict with both versions spelled out,
because this endpoint is what the bind UI polls to decide whether to offer
an Update flow — it should not have to infer `bound_version` from a ref it
also has to parse.

LoopConfigPut.title: LoopConfigPut
LoopConfigPut.description:
Merge onto the board's stored config: exactly the operator fields plus
the optimistic lock.

extra="forbid" rejects unknown keys (typo protection — a silently dropped
`max_iteration` would leave the real cap at its default) AND the
server-owned stop metadata fields and updated_at, which are never
accepted from clients. Omitted fields (and explicit JSON nulls — both
decode to None here) inherit the board's CURRENT value via
canonicalize_loop_config; only the first-ever PUT for a board has no
stored config to inherit from and sees the documented defaults instead.
Bounds live in loop_config_validation.

`version` is the one server-owned key a client MAY send, because GET /loop
returns it and the natural round-trip is to hand it straight back: it is
accepted as an alias for `expected_version` (R14 friction log, card
d8cbbec6). Both names mean the same optimistic-lock precondition and are
normalized to `expected_version` before the service sees the body, so the
alias is read as a precondition and never stored — the server's counter
stays authoritative. Sending both with DIFFERENT values is rejected rather
than silently resolved: picking a winner could skip the lock the caller
thought they had.

LoopConfigRead.title: LoopConfigRead
LoopConfigRead.description:
The complete wire object — every field always present.

The runner json.Unmarshals this without defaults, so a missing numeric
would decode as 0 and trip a safety rail. `updated_at` is served verbatim
as the stored ISO string.

LoopHistoryRead.title: LoopHistoryRead
LoopHistoryRead.description:
Cross-run continuity aggregate (GET /loop/history).

iteration_count is ALL-TIME (numbering stays monotonic across the
board's life); spent_usd sums structured cost_usd SINCE budget_epoch
(all-time when null — conservative). Aggregated server-side because the
executions list endpoint is limit-capped and a lower-bound sum on money
would under-enforce the budget rail.

LoopReadinessRead.title: LoopReadinessRead
LoopReadinessRead.description:
Board-level starvation probe (GET /loop/readiness).

A pure board read — served even before the board's first PUT /loop, so the
runner's pre-flight can never confuse "nothing configured" (404, fatal on
GET /loop) with "nothing to do" (actionable=false here).

LoopStatePatch.title: LoopStatePatch
LoopStatePatch.description:
Runner state transition with an optional, closed stop-reason contract.

``reason`` remains required as the exact legacy fallback. New runners may
additionally send one recognized code with its exact parameter shape. A
malformed structured reason is rejected so the runner can retry the old
``{enabled, reason}`` payload instead of persisting ambiguous metadata.

LoopStatusRead.title: LoopStatusRead
LoopStatusRead.description:
Loop truth layer (GET /loop/status).

One answer to "what is the loop actually doing right now?" — config,
in-flight iterations, and bound-agent liveness stitched server-side so the
frontend never has to. Unconfigured IS a state (`off`), never a 404: the
dashboard must render every board's loop state without special-casing.

state: off (config absent or disabled — wins even over an in-flight
iteration), running (in-flight loop_iteration on this board), parked
(a bound, alive agent last heartbeated loop_state=parked FOR THIS BOARD),
waiting (enabled + a bound agent alive), unattended (enabled + nobody
alive). Parked outranks waiting but never off or running, and expires with
the reporting agent's liveness — that is what keeps parked distinguishable
from a runner that simply died.
Bound = member of an AgentTeam with this board_id — never derived from
health_current_board_id (that's an agent passing through, not a binding).

LoopTemplateDetailRead.title: LoopTemplateDetailRead
LoopTemplateDetailRead.description: One template with its full content — the manager's editing payload.

LoopTemplateFitApplyRead.title: LoopTemplateFitApplyRead
LoopTemplateFitApplyRead.description:
The refreshed report plus a per-fix ledger.

Extends the read model rather than wrapping it: the UI redraws the same
checklist component from either response, and a different shape here would
make applying a fix a second rendering path.

LoopTemplateFitApplyRequest.title: LoopTemplateFitApplyRequest
LoopTemplateFitApplyRequest.description:
Which advertised fixes to run. Ids come verbatim from a fit report's
`fix_id`, so the client never composes one itself.

LoopTemplateFitApplyResult.title: LoopTemplateFitApplyResult
LoopTemplateFitApplyResult.description:
What one fix did. `skipped_already_satisfied` is a SUCCESS — it is the
answer a retry, a double-click, and a stale report all deserve — while
`rejected` means the fix could not run and says why in `detail`.

LoopTemplateFitCheck.title: LoopTemplateFitCheck
LoopTemplateFitCheck.description:
One setup-contract requirement, judged against this board.

`status` separates "the operator must act" from "worth knowing":
`missing` is reserved for requirements a fix can repair, so the UI's
one-click affordance and the severity never disagree. `fix_id` is the
handle p2-02's apply endpoint takes, and encodes its own argument
(`create_column:done`) so applying needs no second lookup.

LoopTemplateFitRead.title: LoopTemplateFitRead
LoopTemplateFitRead.description:
What a board HAS vs what a template NEEDS, plus pre-filled slots.

Open like `LoopBindingRead`: the bind step grows (p2-02 adds applied-fix
results, p3 adds UI hints) and a closed model would make each addition a
coordinated schema change.

LoopTemplateLintRead.title: LoopTemplateLintRead
LoopTemplateLintRead.description:
Repo-fact leak warnings for one template (spec F12).

Wrapped in an object rather than served as a bare list so the response can
grow a summary or a rule version without breaking callers — and so an empty
result reads as `{"findings": []}`, which a UI can distinguish from a
failed request more easily than `[]`.

Never an error shape: findings are hints and the endpoint is always 200.

LoopTemplatePreviewRead.title: LoopTemplatePreviewRead
LoopTemplatePreviewRead.description:
Exactly what the runner would receive, plus why.

`loop_prompt_with_tools_manifest` is the string the AGENT reads: the runner
appends its tools manifest after rendering, so a preview showing only
`loop_prompt` would be missing the block that tells the agent what it may
call. Both are served because the manager's editor pane shows the authored
prompt while the bind step shows the runner view.

`findings` never blocks — a preview that 422'd would hide the very problems
the operator opened it to see. Errors belong on PUT /loop.

LoopTemplateProfileRead.title: LoopTemplateProfileRead
LoopTemplateProfileRead.description: The profile page: stored identity + derived track record + contract.

LoopTemplatePublishRead.title: LoopTemplatePublishRead
LoopTemplatePublishRead.description:
The published template plus any repo-fact leak warnings (spec F12).

A subclass rather than a `warnings` field on the detail shape itself: every
read route returns that shape, and an always-empty key there would advertise
a scan those routes do not run. Publish is the one moment a kernel becomes
something boards RUN and exports can carry, so it is the one response that
carries the findings. They never block — the publish already happened.

LoopTemplateTrackRecord.title: LoopTemplateTrackRecord
LoopTemplateTrackRecord.description:
Derived from stamped executions — never stored, so it cannot drift.

Every outcome bucket is always present (a zero is a fact, not a missing
key), and `unknown` holds iterations written before the runner's
`outcome=` convention or by a run that never reported one.

LoopTemplateTrackRecordBoard.title: LoopTemplateTrackRecordBoard
LoopTemplateTrackRecordBoard.description: One board's share of a template's history.

LoopTemplateUpdate.title: LoopTemplateUpdate
LoopTemplateUpdate.description:
Every field optional — this is the autosave path.

`expected_updated_at` is the draft's optimistic lock, and the value it is
compared against is `draft_updated_at` from the read shapes — never their
`updated_at`, which tracks the whole row on a different clock. It is
optional so the first save after a load, and every non-UI caller, need not
carry one; when present it must match the token the caller was handed.

LoopTransitionPage.title: LoopTransitionPage
LoopTransitionPage.description:
`total` is the unpaged count so the UI can render "showing N of M"
without walking every page to find out how deep the history goes.

LoopTransitionRead.title: LoopTransitionRead
LoopTransitionRead.description:
One enable/disable on the board's loop timeline.

`source` is the attribution the UI renders and is derived server-side from
which credential made the call — "runner" when an agent API key did it,
"human" otherwise — so the frontend never has to infer intent from a
reason string.

repo_url.title: Repo Url
repo_url.description: The git remote at this root. Without it, this mapping's content level and enabled state cannot carry over to the repository's auto-match on a reconnected device.

content_level.title: Content Level
content_level.description: Omitted: `rich` where rich capture is enabled, otherwise `standard`.

MappingEffectiveCapture.title: MappingEffectiveCapture
MappingEffectiveCapture.description:
What a mapping captures: the owner's choice and what this device and
server can honour. A rich mapping on a device without rich capture
captures `full` (never more than chosen) and says why.

MergeQueueReEnqueueRequest.title: MergeQueueReEnqueueRequest
MergeQueueReEnqueueRequest.description:
PAR-3c: re-queue an existing entry by its parent card_id.

The consolidator pipeline calls this once it has resolved the conflict;
the worker then re-attempts the merge. No repo / pr fields — the entry
already has them.

lifecycle.title: Lifecycle
lifecycle.description: Generic lifecycle steps for the runner walker (lane A.2).

NoteAppend.title: NoteAppend
NoteAppend.description:
Body for a surgical append: new blocks only, never the whole document.

Unlike `NoteUpdate.content`, this field is required and must carry at least
one block. An append that normalizes to an empty doc means the caller lost
its payload — surfacing that as 422 beats a silent no-op the operator would
have to notice by diffing the note.

NoteFormat.title: NoteFormat
NoteFormat.description:
Wire format for a single note read. `prosemirror` (default) returns the
stored canonical PM JSON; `markdown` serializes it back to CommonMark.

NoteSectionReplace.title: NoteSectionReplace
NoteSectionReplace.description:
Body for a surgical section replace: the anchor to find, the body to put
under it.

Unlike `NoteAppend`, empty content is ACCEPTED — "this section has nothing in
it yet" is a legitimate intent for a tracker, and unlike an append it cannot
silently lose a payload (the caller named the section it meant to clear).
A blank anchor is rejected: it identifies nothing, and reading it as "the
whole document" would turn a surgical tool into a full-body overwrite.

NotificationPreferenceRead.title: NotificationPreferenceRead
NotificationPreferenceRead.description:
Raw prefs (the user's stored knobs) plus the resolved `effective` map the
FE renders the grid from: category -> {channel_key: bool}. The effective map
is total over CATEGORY_DEFAULTS × registered channels so the grid stays
data-driven (a new channel/category needs no FE change).

OrphanInfo.title: OrphanInfo
OrphanInfo.description:
A dangling edge: one endpoint is not a live card on this board (e.g. a
cross-board reference). `*_on_board` flags say which endpoint is missing.

PairingCodeRequest.title: PairingCodeRequest
PairingCodeRequest.description:
The code travels in the body so it never lands in a URL or access log.
Anything that is not a code answers like an unknown code (404), not 422.

PairingGrant.title: PairingGrant
PairingGrant.description: Returned exactly once per pairing; a replay is `expired_token`.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name the device asked for; null means the neutral `platform-arch-<id8>` default is used on approval.

device_code.title: Device Code
device_code.description: Secret; only the device keeps it and polls with it.

PromptConfigSummary.title: PromptConfigSummary
PromptConfigSummary.description: Lightweight prompt config for the composite response.

PromptStageDefault.title: PromptStageDefault
PromptStageDefault.description: Metadata + default content for a prompt stage.

RedactionFact.title: RedactionFact
RedactionFact.description:
That the secret filter ran and how often it replaced text; what it
removed is never kept.

RhythmBucket.title: RhythmBucket
RhythmBucket.description:
Timeline entries that began in [t, t + bucket_seconds), each counted
once as one kind, in this order of precedence: prompt, error (a failed
call), work (an MCP call that touched a card or note you can see), file
(an edit, write or patch), tool (any other call).

RhythmLane.title: RhythmLane
RhythmLane.description: A subagent session, drawn from its first to its last event.

RichCaptureOffer.title: RichCaptureOffer
RichCaptureOffer.description:
DevicePolicy.rich_capture: present only when this server accepts rich
capture and the device declared RICH_CAPTURE_CAPABILITY. The device uses
the smaller of these limits and its own, and captures rich only for the
mappings listed.

RichCaptureStatus.title: RichCaptureStatus
RichCaptureStatus.description:
DeviceStatusReport.rich_capture: sent only to a server that offered
rich capture (older servers forbid the member).

RichIngestResult.title: RichIngestResult
RichIngestResult.description:
IngestResult plus one ContentAck per declaration of every acknowledged
record, repeated when the record is replayed so a device that lost an
ack can resume. A record ack never settles its bodies. A rejected record
gets no content acks: its rejection settles every declaration it carried,
and the device deletes their spooled bodies.

RichMappingGrant.title: RichMappingGrant
RichMappingGrant.description:
A mapping this device may capture rich, since when on the server's
clock. `rich_since` is part of the device's capture settings, so leaving
and re-entering rich (even between two policy fetches) starts a new
generation, and the server rejects content observed before it.

SensorManifestEntry.title: SensorManifestEntry
SensorManifestEntry.description:
Manifest of a sensor reported by a Go agent via heartbeat.

Mirrors harness.SensorManifestEntry on the agent side — the platform
treats agents as the source of truth for which sensors are installed.

key.title: Key
key.description: Opaque; pass to GET …/calls/{key} to expand.

turn_index.title: Turn Index
turn_index.description: 0 before the first prompt; each prompt opens the next turn.

name.title: Name
name.description: Tool name, or the event action without one.

duration_ms.title: Duration Ms
duration_ms.description: From the call's first to last event, or as the agent reported it; null for a call captured as a single event.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: From the call's own completion signals only: failed when any event failed, succeeded when one completed; otherwise running while the session is still open, or unknown once it has ended. Null for prompts and subagents.

args_preview.title: Args Preview
args_preview.description: The command or arguments as sent, cut to 300 characters; null when not sent (see withheld) or absent.

prompt_preview.title: Prompt Preview
prompt_preview.description: A prompt's text as sent, cut to 1000 characters.

output.title: Output
output.description: Whether the call's output reached Backplane. Output is never in this page; expand the call to read it.

withheld.title: Withheld
withheld.description: Content this call had but its capture level did not send.

work_refs.title: Work Refs
work_refs.description: Cards and notes this MCP call changed or consulted that still exist where you can see them.

subagent.description: The child session, for kind subagent.

SessionCallItem.title: SessionCallItem
SessionCallItem.description:
One timeline entry: a prompt, a tool call (every event sharing its
native call id), or a subagent session placed at its start.

turns.title: Turns
turns.description: Totals for each turn that has an item on this page, counted over the whole turn.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: The page of earlier items; the first page is the newest.

relation.title: Relation
relation.description: changed when the session changed it at least once.

cost_usd.title: Cost Usd
cost_usd.description: Effective USD cost: per usage report the agent-reported cost when it reported one, otherwise Backplane's API list-price estimate; null when neither exists (never 0 for unknown).

cost_source.title: Cost Source
cost_source.description: Where cost_usd came from: all agent-reported, all estimated, or mixed.

cost_basis.title: Cost Basis
cost_basis.description: spend when an API key (or enterprise contract) paid; api_equivalent for a subscription or unknown login, where the cost is what the same usage would cost at API list price, not money spent. Null without a cost.

stale_usage_count.title: Stale Usage Count
stale_usage_count.description: Rows estimated under an older price table than price_table_version, awaiting a reprice.

SessionModelUsage.title: SessionModelUsage
SessionModelUsage.description:
A session's usage reports for one model, provider, service tier and
auth kind. Token buckets are disjoint except reasoning_tokens, which is
part of output_tokens.

live_count.title: Live Count
live_count.description: Sessions whose display_state is active right now.

wall_duration_seconds.title: Wall Duration Seconds
wall_duration_seconds.description: Elapsed time covered by at least one session: the union of each session's span from first to last event, cut to start at `since`, so overlapping sessions and subagent threads count once.

reasoning_tokens.title: Reasoning Tokens
reasoning_tokens.description: Part of output_tokens spent reasoning; not added to totals.

cost_api_equivalent_usd.title: Cost Api Equivalent Usd
cost_api_equivalent_usd.description: Summed effective cost of sessions under a subscription or an unknown login: what the usage would cost at API list price, not money spent. Null when none of them has a cost. Never added to cost_spend_usd.

cost_spend_usd.title: Cost Spend Usd
cost_spend_usd.description: Summed effective cost of sessions an API key or enterprise contract paid for. Null when none of them has a cost.

cost_complete.title: Cost Complete
cost_complete.description: False when any session that used tokens has no cost or an unpriced usage report, so the costs are a lower bound.

SessionPeriodSummary.title: SessionPeriodSummary
SessionPeriodSummary.description: Totals across your sessions matching the list filters it was asked for.

end.title: End
end.description: Now while the session is open (`live`), else its last event.

bucket_seconds.title: Bucket Seconds
bucket_seconds.description: Width of each bucket; 0 for a session with a single instant.

idle_spans.title: Idle Spans
idle_spans.description: Silences longer than 5 minutes between activity events, plus the current one up to `end` while the session is live.

capture_gaps.title: Capture Gaps
capture_gaps.description: Records ingest rejected; where in time they fell is unknown.

price_table_version.title: Price Table Version
price_table_version.description: Version of the vendored price tables estimates are made from.

SkillVersionRead.title: SkillVersionRead
SkillVersionRead.description: Version metadata; file contents ride version detail and diff responses.

TeamMembershipInfoCompat.title: TeamMembershipInfoCompat
TeamMembershipInfoCompat.description: Backward-compat: singular role for legacy consumers.

UploadSlot.title: UploadSlot
UploadSlot.description: Where an upload stands; chunks are PUT by index, in any order.

bytes.title: Bytes
bytes.description: Size of what was not sent, when the device or server recorded it.

WorkspaceSummaryTrimmedActivity.title: WorkspaceSummaryTrimmedActivity
WorkspaceSummaryTrimmedActivity.description:
`?summary_activity=true` variant: the same digest with the embedded
activity rows stripped of their JSONB snapshots. The dashboard renders
id/entity_type/summary only, but MCP get_workspace_summary forwards this
payload verbatim to an agent, so the trim is opt-in like everywhere else.

app__schemas__notes__note__NoteSummary.title: NoteSummary
app__schemas__notes__note__NoteSummary.description:
List-view note WITHOUT the heavy `content` field.

Returned by the list endpoints when `?summary_only=true` — cures a real
72KB-for-4-notes payload overflow where a board view only needs titles and
metadata, not every note's full PM document.

`preview` gives the list back the one thing dropping `content` cost it: a
glance at what the note says. It is the same text server-side search
matches (see services.notes.content_text), so a search hit always shows
the operator something recognizable.
